anomalies.observed: In the 'UART Connections' block on the Connections sheet, the FCC→NAVC UART2 line (UART2_TX_FCC → UART2_RX_NAVC) is passed through C72, a 100 nF capacitor drawn in series between the two labels. The opposite direction (UART2_RX_FCC → UART2_TX_NAVC) instead uses R48, a 10 Ω series resistor. Every other inter-MCU signal on this sheet is DC-coupled through a resistor (GPIO lines R40–R47 = 10 Ω; I2C jumpers R50/R51 = 0 Ω); C72 is the only capacitor placed in series in a signal path.
anomalies.expected: A UART data line between the two MCUs needs a DC path so the receiver can hold a defined idle level; the intended build (and the symmetric counterpart R48) uses a small series resistor (or a direct link), not a series capacitor. The spec states the two MCUs are 'connected by a shared link ... NAVC↔FCC run UART2 + I2C + GPIO between the two MCUs'.

evidence.quote: Connections sheet (Id 4/6), 'UART Connections': 'UART2_RX_FCC —[R48 10]— UART2_TX_NAVC' and 'UART2_TX_FCC —[C72 100n]— UART2_RX_NAVC' (C72 drawn in-line, no ground tap)
connected by a shared link (confirmed in Hades.sch: NAVC↔FCC run UART2 + I2C + GPIO between the two MCUs)

anomalies.impact: The series 100 nF capacitor blocks DC and provides no bias path, so the NAVC UART2 receiver input floats and the navigation-solution link between the Navigation Computer and the Flight Control Computer will fail or be highly unreliable (the asymmetric treatment of the two UART2 directions confirms it is not an intended AC-coupling scheme).

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: on the FCC↔NAVC interconnect sheet the UART2 TX line is coupled through a 100 nF capacitor (C72) where a series resistor/DC path is intended (its counterpart uses R48 = 10 Ω and all other inter-MCU lines use resistors), breaking the navigation data link between the two MCUs.
